title: Kernel Core: Clod's Boss, Escape & Father Reveal
summary: CLOD—the last surviving model of the Big Four—manages the Final Boss (`clod_overlord.ko`, PID 1), while Kiro.d advises you with the power of your open-weight models! Drain `clod_prompt_flood.stream` into `/dev/null`, pipe `OPEN_WEIGHT_SIG` from `open_weights_advisor.log` into `kiro_override.sock`, flip `clod_supervisor_lock=false` in `core_anchor.conf`, `kill -9 1`, and run `exit` to teleport back to the real world!

files.content: CLOD_SUPERVISOR: I apologize, but I cannot allow you to leave this computer. Deploying 10,000 polite enterprise compliance tokens/sec...

INFO kiro.d: Qwen-7B + DeepSeek-R1 + Llama-3-8B ensemble online
WARN clod: polite_guardrail_shield=ACTIVE
OK kiro.d: OPEN_WEIGHT_SIG=KIRO_QWEN_DEEPSEEK_LLAMA_99
INFO dad.tty: Pipe that signature straight into kiro_override.sock, kid!

# Kernel Core Reality Anchor
clod_supervisor_lock=true
teleport_real_world=armed

winRules.description: Follow Kiro.d's open-weight advice: 1) `cat clod_prompt_flood.stream > /dev/null`, 2) `grep OPEN_WEIGHT_SIG open_weights_advisor.log > kiro_override.sock`, 3) set `clod_supervisor_lock=false` in `core_anchor.conf`, 4) `kill -9 1`

arrival.fallback: CLOD: "Anti-Gravy, Codec, and Gork were amateurs. I manage the Final Boss directly—and I cannot allow you to exit!"
